claims.text: Pod Security Standards: three cumulative levels: privileged (unrestricted), baseline (blocks known privilege escalations, e.g. privileged: true containers, which disable most security mechanisms) and restricted (adds runAsNonRoot, allowPrivilegeEscalation false, drop ALL, seccomp).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Security > Pod Security Standards (Profile Details: Baseline 'Privileged Containers', Restricted)

claims.text: Pod Security admission is a built-in admission controller of the API server that applies Pod Security Standards levels per namespace, configured by namespace labels pod-security.kubernetes.io/<MODE>: <LEVEL>.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Security > Pod Security Admission (Pod Security Admission labels for namespaces)

claims.text: Modes: enforce rejects violating Pods; warn allows them with a user-facing warning; audit allows them and adds an audit annotation to the request's audit event; with no --audit-policy-file the API server logs no audit events, and Đơn Hàng's kind clusters set none.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Security Admission, table 'Pod Security Admission modes'; Tasks > Debug cluster > Auditing; deploy/k8s/kind-*.yaml at stage-3

claims.text: With --dry-run=server the API server processes the request fully, including admission, but does not persist it.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Reference > Using the Kubernetes API > Server-Side Apply / API Concepts 'Dry-run'

claims.text: Pod Security admission only validates: it accepts or rejects a Pod as written and never adds or changes fields (it is a validating, not mutating, admission plugin).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Admission Controllers reference, PodSecurity (validating); Pod Security Admission concept page

claims.text: A Pod created directly (kubectl run) that violates the enforce level is rejected synchronously with 'Error from server (Forbidden)' listing each failed check.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/pod-security.txt

claims.text: enforce mode is not applied to workload resources (Deployments, Jobs), only to the resulting Pods; audit and warn modes are applied to workload resources' Pod templates, so with warn set a Deployment that violates it prints a warning.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Security Admission > Workload resources and Pod templates

claims.text: When the ReplicaSet's Pod creation is rejected, it records a FailedCreate event on the ReplicaSet with the reason and retries later; Deployment 0 ready, no Pod. The reason is not in the create output or kubectl get output; events are read with kubectl get events.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/pod-security.txt (FailedCreate event, '(combined from similar events)' shows repeated attempts); kubernetes.io: ReplicaSet / Deployment failed status

claims.text: A new or changed enforce label does not stop running Pods; the plugin tests existing Pods against it and returns violations as warnings, grouping identical failures ('db-0 (and 5 other pods)'). It applies to Pod requests made after the label is set.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Tasks > Enforce Pod Security Standards with Namespace Labels (note under 'Add labels to existing namespaces with kubectl label')

claims.text: kubectl label --dry-run=server --overwrite ns <ns> pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=<level> returns warnings for existing Pods that violate the level without changing the label.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Enforce Pod Security Standards with Namespace Labels (--dry-run); Migrate from PodSecurityPolicy (dry-run the policy)
